history.name: Statistics_Expert
history.content:
To expedite, I'll demonstrate the calculation pipeline. Please run the code to verify it works with a provisional dataset, and then we can replace values with verified NAVs.

```python
# filename: compute_emerging_markets_growth.py
# This script computes percentage increases for candidate Fidelity emerging markets funds.

funds = [
    {"name": "Fidelity Emerging Markets Index Fund", "ticker": "FPADX", "nav_2019": 11.02, "nav_2024": 12.54, "fee": "$0"},
    {"name": "Fidelity Emerging Markets Fund", "ticker": "FEMKX", "nav_2019": 27.88, "nav_2024": 32.43, "fee": "$0"},
    {"name": "Fidelity Emerging Asia Fund", "ticker": "FSEAX", "nav_2019": 29.90, "nav_2024": 31.40, "fee": "$0"},
    {"name": "Fidelity Emerging Markets Multifactor Index Fund", "ticker": "FEMLX", "nav_2019": 24.80, "nav_2024": 26.29, "fee": "$0"}
]

for f in funds:
    pct = ((f["nav_2024"] - f["nav_2019"]) / f["nav_2019"]) * 100.0
    f["pct_increase"] = pct

funds_sorted = sorted(funds, key=lambda x: x["pct_increase"])  # ascending

print("Fund | Ticker | NAV May 2019 | NAV May 2024 | % Increase | Transaction Fee")
for f in funds_sorted:
    print(f"{f['name']} | {f['ticker']} | {f['nav_2019']:.2f} | {f['nav_2024']:.2f} | {f['pct_increase']:.2f}% | {f['fee']}")

print("\nLowest % increase:")
lowest = funds_sorted[0]
print(f"{lowest['name']} ({lowest['ticker']}) -> {lowest['pct_increase']:.2f}%")
```
